verdict.rationale: RustDesk documents a free, open-source ID/rendezvous (hbbs) and relay (hbbr) server you deploy on your own infrastructure via a provided compose.yml and `docker compose up -d`, and you can also host the web client on your own domain. Several users report running their own lookup/relay servers successfully for years, though some found self-hosting difficult or laggy. missing for 10: authentication and a web console/access control in the free self-hosted server (one user reports zero auth, and these features are listed under Server Pro), and consistent reports of easy setup (some users call it nearly impossible or unusable).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: Server OSS: a free, open-source ID/rendezvous server (hbbs) and relay server (hbbr) that you can deploy on your own infrastructure.
Host the web client on your server with your domain name to make remote access even easier.
You can use our rendezvous/relay server, [set up your own](https://rustdesk.com/server)
Has used it for years with their own lookup/relay server and says it keeps getting better.
